promises.quote: The access of Medacs Policies and Procedures to Medacs staff | was also concerned to hear that | was not aware of the Medacs Epilepsy Policy. He said in evidence that he had no specific recollection of the epilepsy policy, but he was aware that the Medacs policies were available in a 'loose leaf binder in most custody suites'. Asa very experienced FME J gave evidence that he had been asked to review most of the policies, but he could not specifically recall this one
promises.summary: Staff training on Medacs policies and procedures, including location and sign-off

promises.quote: | have an ongoing review of divisional policing entitled 'Transforming Divisional Policing' which looks at all aspects of improving the operational service we provide. | have specifically asked it to look at finding ways of processing detainees with greater efficiency in order to reduce their periods of detention,
promises.summary: Ongoing review to improve detainee processing efficiency

promises.quote: GMP has reviewed its arrangements for communication between custody and clinical staff to negate the practice of MEDACs staff working on two separate records of notes and to improve the continuity of care provided to detainees with health needs
promises.summary: Improved communication between custody and clinical staff

promises.quote: We already have a process that checks custody records to ensure visits are timely and carried out in accordance with the sergeant's risk assessment
promises.summary: Process to check custody records for timely visits

promises.quote: Since the death of Mr Salton, Custody Branch has significantly upgraded its ICIS computer system. This system prompts Custody Sergeants to undertake further reviews linked to specific/significant events affecting the detainees period of detention, including an exit risk assessment
promises.summary: Upgraded ICIS system to prompt reviews of risk assessments

promises.quote: We have conducted a review of handovers between sergeants. As a result we have made it clear to sergeants that the handover need not be a comprehensive review of each detainee. Rather, they should have completed the Custody Summary Screen so that all the relevant detail is available on the ICIS system and the handover should contain key risk issues, for example medical conditions, medication required and so forth
promises.summary: Clear handover policy requiring Custody Summary Screen completion

promises.quote: Since your observations we have put out improved guidance on completion of the PER form to sergeants which include what to record, when it is to be done and how it is to be signed off
promises.summary: Improved guidance for PER form completion

concerns.quote: During the course of the evidence | heard that Mr Salton had remained in custody overnight and was not progressed as quickly as he could have | been whilst in custody as there was no-one available to interview him. This is as a result of GMP policy on how people are progressed through custody. The Prisoner Processing Unit is not staffed overnight which leads to people being in custody longer than they should be and bringing GMP

There was a lack of understanding amongst the custody staff and staff from other agencies as to the level of observations Mr Salton was on and why he was on those observations. It is important that everyone who | has care of someone in custody understands what the observations have | been, what they should be, when they are to be carried out, whether rousing is required and why the observaticns are set as they are - i.e. what the medical condition/ concern is.
When the deceased is visited and checked all such visits should be | accurately recorded on the custody record
Risk assessments carried out whilst in police custody should be recorded when they are done. If there are no changes to a risk assessment then this should be recorded and any rationale noted.

Handovers between Custody Sergeants were ineffective and there was no handover between the Civilian Detention Staff. important information was missed or iost in translation. Proper handovers should take place as to a detained person's condition, risk assessment, any medical condition, level of visits and other important matters.
The Prisoner Escort Form was incorrectly completed. The final Custody Sergeant should ensure that the transferring documentation is accurate.

promises.quote: The CPS Operations Directorate has also been considering the national implications and as a result ensured we have modified CPS training so advocates conducting youth court cases are reminded that a youth can always be remanded for their "own welfare
promises.summary: Modified CPS training to remind advocates that youths can be remanded for welfare

concerns.quote: recent changes to legislation means that whilst in custody 17 year olds are now treated as children for the purposes of the Police and Criminal Evidence Act (PACE). However the failure to make legislative changes to the supporting legislation means that for 17 year olds there is an anomaly in the system particularly around the provision of accommodation for a 17 year old who is refused bail
concerns.hazard: 17 year olds denied accommodation when refused bail

concerns.quote: across Greater Manchester it is estimated that, until recently, in only 10% of cases where the police requested such a service from a local authority a bed was available
concerns.hazard: lack of accommodation for children under 17

concerns.quote: Greater Manchester Police have implemented a system to try and ensure that this situation does not happen again. It was therefore decided to hold a joint medical and police exit risk assessment when someone who has displayed self- harm ideation or behaviour leaves custody
concerns.hazard: absence of exit risk assessments for self-harm cases

concerns.quote: There was a failure by Lancashire to note her move which led to a delay in her case being transferred, but in addition there was a failure in the communications with Tameside for each team to understand what was being requested and to have oversight of the situation
concerns.hazard: communication breakdown between youth offending teams

concerns.quote: No intelligence was placed on Kesia's nominal profile despite a number of concerning contacts with her by officers

The Inquest heard a great deal of evidence from officers as to their understanding and actions. No intelligence was placed on Kesia's nominal profile despite a number of concerning contacts with her by officers. It is a core function of the police to submit such intelligence
concerns.hazard: lack of safeguarding protocol for non-criminal concerns

links.explanation: Both reports highlight shortcomings in how risk assessments are managed during police custody. The earlier report stresses the need to record assessments promptly, while the later report calls for a joint medical‑police exit assessment for detainees showing self‑harm.
